llm.summary: This skill is a narrowly scoped helper for querying public Apple job postings through the disclosed Crawlora API, with some implementation issues users should understand.

dimensions.detail: External HTTPS requests to api.crawlora.net and use of CRAWLORA_API_KEY are clearly disclosed and proportionate to the API-integration purpose, though the API key is written into a temporary curl config file without explicit character validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency installation, startup hook, or system modification is present; the artifact consists of markdown reference files and one shell helper.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are focused on using scripts/crawlora.sh and the helper restricts paths to /apple-jobs/job and /apple-jobs/search, but it permits POST even though the documented endpoints are GET-only.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The helper creates a temporary curl config with chmod 600 and removes it on exit; no sudo, root execution, background service, scheduled task, or persistent credential storage was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Apple jobs research, and the artifact only documents two Apple Jobs endpoints for search and job detail via Crawlora.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Reasonable to install if you intend to use Crawlora for Apple jobs research. Set CRAWLORA_API_KEY only from a trusted source, avoid passing sensitive personal data in search parameters, and prefer an updated version that validates the API key value and removes unsupported POST handling.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Use of a shell helper is disclosed in SKILL.md and the script narrows the remote host and paths; absence of richer permission metadata is a packaging limitation rather than evidence of hidden authority.
[E1] expected: The external transmission findings correspond to the documented Crawlora API calls needed for the skill's purpose; the destination is fixed to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 and the data involved is user-supplied job search parameters or job ids.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 operation restricts a temporary credential config file and does not invoke sudo, root, or privilege escalation.
[T09] unexpected: The curl config construction uses CRAWLORA_API_KEY without validating characters, which is a real hardening issue if an attacker can control the environment value, but normal operation sends the key only to the fixed, declared Crawlora service.
[T09] unexpected: The helper allows POST to the two allowlisted Apple Jobs paths even though reference/endpoints.md lists both routes as GET-only; this is unnecessary API surface but remains confined to the declared host and paths.
